thread.title: ETF Closing Report: ETFs, Stocks Set to Close Higher as Tech Sector Drives Gains; Traders Await Iran Decision

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Closing Report: ETFs, Stocks Set to Close Higher as Tech Sector Drives Gains; Traders Await Iran Decision
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Monday's ahead of the session's close:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.4%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.5%
PowerShares QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +0.9%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.8%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): -1.3%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were modestly lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 0.9%.
U.S. stocks were mostly higher as the sesison prepares to close, with the technology sector propping up the major indices, led by a record high in shares of component stock Apple (AAPL) and strength in chipmakers. Apple shares were building on Friday's rally after Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.A, BRK.B) Warren Buffet heaped more praise on the company.
Geopolitical issues were also at the forefront, with President Donald Trump considering whether the U.S. should end its participation in the Iranian nuclear deal before Saturday. Media reports are saying Trump would announce the government's decision on Iran on Tuesday, 2 pm ET.
In economic data, March consumer credit rose $11.62 billion, missing the $15.6 billion consensus with the previous print revised up to $13.64 billion versus a $10.6 billion February gain.
Power Play: Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.3% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.4%.
Athenahealth (ATHN) rose more than 15% after the company said it will study an unsolicited proposal received Monday by Elliott Management to buy the company for $160 a share and an enterprise value of about $6.9 billion, which the latter said could be increased after private diligence. The activist fund founded by Paul Singer said in a letter that athenahealth's stock has underperformed because of factors including "poor execution, significant management turnover, inefficient allocation of resources and the loss of strategic focus." Elliott said athenahealth's cost-reduction plan was a "well-intentioned first step" that has suffered from flaws, and recent leadership changes have fallen short of what investors expected. The company also "refused to engage" with Elliott when it made a private approach last year, the fund said.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.8%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 2.1% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2%.
Billionaire investor Carl Icahn has sold his take in American International Group (AIG) after being associated with one of the biggest U.S. property and casualty insurers for more than two years, according to media reports on Monday, citing sources familiar with the matter. Icahn started buying AIG shares in 2015 and became its third-largest investor with a 4.76% stake at the end of 2017. However, Icahn had already started planning to sell his stake in AIG last year after it became evident the company would name Brian Duperreault, who would oppose demands to break up AIG, as its new CEO, according to a source cited by Reuters. AIG shares rose some 1%.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 09% while other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were higher.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 1.4% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 1.2%.
TowerJazz (TSEM) slumped nearly 9% after the firm reported Q1 adjusted diluted EPS was $0.31, missing Street view of $0.41 and down from $0.49 in the year-ago quarter. Revenues fell year-over-year to $312.7 million from $330.1 million, below the Street view of $325 million. For Q2, the company expects revenues to be $335 million, with an upward or downward range of 5%, representing a sequential growth of 7%. Analysts are expecting revenues of $344 million.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.5% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.3%.
MagneGas (MNGA) rose marginally after the company said it generated record sales of $1.06 million in April, which the company says is the highest combined industrial gas and welding supply sales in its history. According to MagneGas, the record 236% year-over-year growth was largely due to recent acquisitions that expanded the company into California, Louisiana, and Texas, along with accelerated organic growth in Florida.
Commodities
Crude was up 0.1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.3%. Natural gas was up 1% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.8%.
Gold was down 0.03%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was down 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.1%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.8% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were weaker.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.1% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in positive territory.
Del Frisco's Restaurant Group (DFRG) fell some 8% after the restaurant chain reported fiscal Q1 adjusted net profit of $0.10 per share, down from $0.20 per share in the prior year period which came in lower than the $0.19 per share average Street estimate. Revenue for the quarter ended March 27 was $89.3 million, up from $83.9 million reported for the same period last year and higher than the $88.4 million Street estimate. For the fiscal year ending Dec. 25, the company expects adjusted earnings to range from $0.66 to $0.76 per share, and comparable restaurant sales growth of 0% to 2%. The Street estimate calls for earnings of $0.69 per share.
Separately, the company said it has agreed to acquire Barteca Restaurant Group for $325 million in cash. Barteca owns two restaurant brands, Barcelona Wine Bar and Bartaco, with a total of 31 restaurants operating across 10 states. The business generated $127.9 million in net sales in 2017.
